title: LLM 0 to Hero
tagline: From zero knowledge to shipping LLM apps.
description: A 60-card guided run through the exact skills that turn beginners into builders.

modules.title: What LLMs Really Are
modules.summary: The big idea behind the buzz.

cards.content: An LLM is a massive neural net trained to predict the next word in a sentence, nothing more, nothing less.
It doesn’t think. It patterns. Billions of examples taught it what usually comes next.
The magic happens at scale: more parameters, more data, more compute equals shockingly fluent output.
ChatGPT, Claude, Grok — they’re all just really good next-word predictors wrapped in a friendly interface.
LLMs are generalists. One model can write code, translate languages, or draft emails without being retrained.
They run on tokens — tiny chunks of text that the model treats like puzzle pieces.
Size matters. A 7B model fits on your laptop. A 405B model needs a data center.
Open-source models like Llama 3 let anyone run them locally without paying API bills.
The hero path starts here: stop treating them like magic and start seeing them as powerful autocomplete on steroids.
If you remember one thing: LLMs are prediction machines that feel intelligent because language is the ultimate pattern.

modules.title: LLM Mechanics
modules.summary: How the prediction engine actually ticks.

cards.content: Every LLM starts with a transformer architecture that lets it look at the entire conversation at once.
Attention is the secret sauce: the model decides which earlier words matter most for predicting the next one.
Layers stack on layers. Early ones catch basic grammar, later ones grasp meaning and intent.
Parameters are the adjustable knobs — 70 billion of them in a decent model, each tuned during training.
Inference is when the model runs live: you type, it predicts, token by token, until it stops.
Temperature controls creativity. Low for precise answers, high for wild ideas.
Context window is the memory limit. New models remember 128k tokens — roughly an entire book.
Embeddings turn your words into numbers so the math-loving model can work with them.
Sampling picks the next token. Greedy grabs the most likely; top-p keeps it diverse.
The whole thing is just statistics at planetary scale, yet it feels like talking to a genius.

modules.title: Training Basics
modules.summary: How raw models become super useful.

cards.content: Pre-training is the first phase: the model reads the entire internet to learn language patterns.
Next-token prediction is the only teacher. No labels needed — just massive text and a simple goal.
Fine-tuning comes after: smaller datasets teach the model to follow instructions or stay on-topic.
RLHF adds human feedback so the model prefers helpful, honest, and harmless answers.
LoRA is the cheat code: tweak just a tiny fraction of parameters instead of retraining everything.
Quantization shrinks models so a 70B beast runs on consumer hardware without losing much smarts.
Data quality beats quantity. Clean, diverse, high-signal text makes far better models.
Training costs millions in GPUs, but inference is cheap — that’s why APIs exploded.
Open models let you fine-tune on your own data and keep everything private.
The hero move: you don’t need to train from scratch. Start with a strong base and customize fast.

modules.title: Advanced Techniques
modules.summary: Level-up tricks that separate pros from beginners.

cards.content: Chain-of-thought prompting makes the model think step-by-step and dramatically boosts accuracy.
Few-shot examples inside the prompt teach the model your style without any fine-tuning.
RAG pulls fresh data from your docs or database so the model never hallucinates outdated facts.
Function calling turns the LLM into an agent that can run code, hit APIs, or book your calendar.
Multi-agent setups let different LLMs debate or divide tasks like a tiny startup team.
Evaluation frameworks catch when the model is confidently wrong before you ship.
Guardrails block toxic output or force the model to say “I don’t know” instead of guessing.
Structured output tools force JSON every time so your app can actually use the response.
Memory layers remember past conversations across sessions without blowing the context window.
These techniques are what turn a simple chatbot into production-grade AI that feels alive.

modules.title: Building LLM Apps
modules.summary: From idea to working product in hours.

cards.content: Start with LangChain or LlamaIndex — they handle the messy plumbing so you focus on the fun stuff.
Build a simple RAG chatbot in under 50 lines of code that answers questions about your own docs.
Add tools so your app can search the web, send emails, or update a spreadsheet automatically.
Host on Vercel or Railway and give your friends a shareable link in minutes.
Use OpenAI, Anthropic, or Grok APIs first — then swap to local models when you want zero cost.
Stream responses so users see text appear live instead of staring at a loading spinner.
Track costs per user so you don’t wake up to a surprise $800 OpenAI bill.
A/B test prompts like you would any product feature — small changes can double quality.
Ship fast, then iterate. The first version will feel magical even if it’s rough around the edges.
Your first LLM app will change how you think about software forever.

modules.title: Hero Level
modules.summary: The mindset and moves that separate builders from dreamers.

cards.content: Treat the model as a junior teammate: great at drafting, terrible at final decisions.
Always add human review for anything that touches customers or money.
Monitor what users actually do with your app — that feedback beats any benchmark.
Combine multiple models: cheap one for simple tasks, smart one for the hard stuff.
Keep your prompts in version control like real code so you can roll back disasters.
Build for your own pain first. Solve one annoying problem and the rest flows.
The best LLM apps feel invisible — users just get better results without noticing the AI.
Stay curious. New models drop every month and the hero path is constant experimentation.
Share what you ship. The community moves faster when everyone shows their work.
You’re not replacing yourself. You’re giving every idea superpowers — now go build something only you could imagine.
